scope: Constructor and coordinate-shape invariants covered by the direct geometry tests
The executable constructor example stored in this contract
verification.evidence_ceiling: Named finite geometry cases only; no field-solver, experimental, or release claim is made.
known_limitations: Mesh objects do not by themselves validate a physical field model or device geometry.

identity.definition: Each paired rpts,zpts value defines one point

outputs.name: mesh
outputs.description: Constructed PointsMesh object. Available properties/methods: R: Radial coordinates [m], N; Z: Axial coordinates [m], N
outputs.constraints: Properties expose generated coordinates; field methods require configured or supplied target mesh

preconditions: Inputs satisfy the documented finite cylindrical coordinate and shape contract

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for nonfinite coordinates, mismatched shapes, negative radius, malformed point dimensions, or invalid rectangular bounds/counts.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Direct NumPy coordinate construction or transform exceptions propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; mesh construction and rotation are direct operations.
failure_semantics.partial_results: A failed constructor returns no mesh object.

example.description: Construct one finite cylindrical point and inspect both coordinate arrays.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import PointsMesh

mesh = PointsMesh([0.2], [0.3])
np.testing.assert_allclose(mesh.R, [0.2])
np.testing.assert_allclose(mesh.Z, [0.3])
example.expected: R and Z are one-element float arrays containing 0.2 m and 0.3 m.
